correctness.rationale: The three sequences B,C,c satisfy X_{n+2}=6X_{n+1}-X_n with specified initial values. Classical identities C_n^2=8B_n^2+1 and c_n^2=(C_{2n-1}-1)/2 give first-window sums, and telescoping gives window differences B_k B_{2n+k+2}, 8B_k B_{2n+k+2}, and 8B_k B_{2n+k+1}. Strong-divisibility gcd(B_a,B_b)=B_gcd(a,b) reduces the infinite gcd to explicit gcd of initial sum and a multiple of B_k. Proof then splits primes 2 (B_k and k share exact 2-adic valuation; mod16 normalization), 3 (B_2m has nu3=nu3(2m)+1 and extra 3 for odd multiple of 3 only c), and other odd primes. Thus D_C=gcd(k,B_k); D_B=h/2 for even k otherwise h; D_c=3h if k=3 mod6 otherwise h for every k>=1. Independent exact arithmetic checked all three against 20 actual windows for k=1..59; finite checks corroborate, infinite follows from valuation proof.
